44/G.goal: Describe how the Majuli VR Tour was implemented for head-mounted and mobile devices and how its user experience is evaluated using post-task, post-session, and cybersickness questionnaires.
44/G.achieves: Provides the learner with a concrete example of moving from an XR system design to implemented demos and evaluation instruments, supporting the course's aim to understand and implement XR systems with confidence.

44/O1.goal: Explain how self-report questionnaires are used to evaluate usability and XR discomfort, including post-task, post-session, and simulator-sickness instruments.
44/O1.achieves: Gives the learner a practical set of evaluation measures for judging whether an XR system is usable, satisfying, and comfortable, supporting user-centered implementation and later optimization.

44/O2.goal: Summarize how the Majuli VR Tour was implemented for Oculus Quest and Google Cardboard and what user-experience flows and features those demos provide.
44/O2.achieves: Connects the case-study system design to concrete device-specific implementations and demo interactions, helping the learner understand how an XR system can be built and tested on real hardware.
